subject: Annual renewal pricing — safety-net credit rail & tier reprice
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluebridge.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@bluebridge.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal ask — safety-net credits & tier reprice for increased capacity

David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our product team is ready to expand usage next quarter and we need to lock pricing for the renewal discussion. A few asks from BlueBridge procurement:  

- A temporary price freeze for the first 6 months of the renewal while we migrate heavy traffic.
- A safety-net credit pool to cover up to 25% of month-over-month overages during the migration window (we call this a "safety-net credit rail").
- A reprice on higher-volume tiers if we commit to a projected 30% uplift in average monthly tokens.

We're happy to move to a 12-month term with quarterly true-ups if that helps; procurement would like this structured as a short addendum rather than a full contract rewrite. Attached is our renewal summary and expected traffic profile for Q3–Q4.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer a temporary price hold + safety-net credits, and what an uplift commit looks like from a commercial perspective?

Best,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Procurement, BlueBridge
phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: BlueBridge_Renewal_Request_2027.pdf

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal ask — safety-net credits & tier reprice for increased capacity

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. We're excited about BlueBridge scaling with us. High-level response:

- Temporary price freeze: we can offer a 6-month price hold on agreed rate cards provided we agree an uplift band and a commit floor for the 12-month term (details below).
- Safety-net credit rail: we can set aside an operational credit pool equal to 20% of expected Q3 spend to offset overages during the migration; credits will be consumed in FIFO order against monthly overages and expire at the end of the 6-month freeze.
- Tier reprice for uplift: if BlueBridge commits to a 30% uplift (measured as rolling 90-day average), we can move you to a stepped rate schedule with a 12% effective discount on the higher-volume tiers after the freeze period.

To proceed I need to confirm: (1) target uplift number you expect to hit within 90 days, (2) do you prefer credits as dollar credits or token-credit buckets, and (3) any procurement constraints on how credits are documented (addendum vs PO credit note). We can put a simple addendum in DocuSign that codifies the price hold and credit rail — I'll loop in commercial ops.

If acceptable I will send a formal counter with numbers and a mutual action plan.

— David
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: BlueBridge renewal counter — pricing mechanics & approval needed

Team — forwarding BlueBridge's asks. Key constraints from procurement: they want a 6-month price hold, safety-net credits for migration overages, and a tier reprice if they make a 30% uplift commit.

Proposed commercial structure (numbers are placeholders for approval):
- Term: 12 months, start 2027-07-01.
- Commit: baseline = current ARR equivalent; proposed uplift commit = +30% baseline for the 12-month term; quarterly true-ups.
- Price hold: freeze current list rates for months 1–6 (no retroactive adjustments).
- Safety-net credit rail: credit pool = 20% of projected Q3 spend (estimated $75k) to offset overages; credits consumed against monthly invoices during months 1–6 and expire month 7.
- Tier reprice: if rolling 90-day usage >= 30% uplift, effective discount = 12% on rates for volumes above the current top tier starting month 7.
- Governance: mutual action plan + addendum (credit mechanics, measurement windows, and clawback clause for intentional overprovisioning).

Questions for finance/legal: 1) acceptable to put credits on an addendum (credit memo style) vs. a separate rebate schedule? 2) are we comfortable with a 20% credit pool (impact to margin modeled below)? 3) approval threshold for a 12% discount band.

Attachments: RBWD_SafetyNet_Credit_Rail_v1.xlsx (detailed credit burn model), Mutual_Action_Plan_BlueBridge.xlsx

Marissa — can you run margin impact and confirm if we can sign this as-is? Ben — if finance signs off, I want to send a formal counter and DocuSign addendum by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
David

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: BlueBridge renewal counter — pricing mechanics & approval needed

David/Ben — reviewed the credit model. Finance comments:

- 20% credit pool (estimated $75k) is acceptable if uplift commit is contractually enforceable. We treat credits as amortized discounts across months 1–6 for accounting.
- Addendum vs rebate schedule: recommend addendum that references a credit memo process — keeps procurement happy and avoids a recurring liability line on the main SOW.
- 12% discount band for post-freeze volumes: approved up to 10% without exec sign-off; anything above 10% needs VP approval. 12% requires VP sign-off (Marissa to take to VP if David requests).

Recommendation: offer 10% stepped discount for volumes above the top tier starting month 7 and a 2% uplift to the credit pool (i.e., 22% of projected Q3 spend) as a compromise. If BlueBridge signs the 30% uplift commit, we'll trigger the 10% discount automatically; a one-time review at month 9 to consider bumping to 12% if usage materially exceeds commit.

I will prepare the cost impact slides and a clean addendum template. Ben — can you draft the counter email with the negotiated numbers? If BlueBridge accepts, I'll queue VP approval for the potential 12% escalation language.

— Marissa
VP Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@bluebridge.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@bluebridge.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Counter: Renewal pricing structure & safety-net credit rail (BlueBridge)

Elena/Carlos — thanks for the patience while we modeled this. Attached are the revised terms and a mutual action plan. Summary of the counter-offer: 

- Term: 12 months (2027-07-01 — 2028-06-30) with quarterly true-ups.
- Price hold: 6-month freeze on current rates (months 1–6).
- Safety-net credit rail: 22% credit pool of projected Q3 spend ($82,500) to offset migration overages during months 1–6; credits expire at the end of month 6.
- Uplift commit & tier reprice: if rolling 90-day average usage reaches +30% vs baseline, BlueBridge gets a stepped 10% discount on volumes above the current top tier starting month 7. We will perform a one-time review at month 9 to consider authorizing up to a 12% band if usage substantially exceeds the commit.
- Measurement & governance: rolling 90-day windows, mutual action plan for migration cutover dates, and credit burn reporting attached.

Next steps: I can send a DocuSign addendum that captures the price hold, credit mechanics, and uplift commit language. Please confirm by EOD Thursday if this is acceptable so we can lock the July 1 start.

DocuSign link (draft): https://docusign.com/redwood/BB-134-addendum (placeholder)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RBWD_SafetyNet_Credit_Rail_v1.xlsx, Mutual_Action_Plan_BlueBridge.xlsx
